what_its_for: Lomustine is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of brain tumors and Hodgkin's lymphoma (a type of blood cancer). It works by slowing down or stopping the growth of cancer cells in your body.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule(s) whole with a full glass of water. Take lomustine on an EMPTY STOMACH, at least 2 hours after eating, to help reduce nausea. Take all the capsules needed for your dose at one time on the same day. You may take it at bedtime to help manage nausea and vomiting. IMPORTANT: Only take this medicine once every 6 weeks — do NOT take it more often than prescribed, even if you feel well.
dosing: Your doctor will carefully calculate your exact dose based on your body size (height and weight) and blood test results. A typical dose is taken just ONCE every 6 weeks (one cycle). Your dose may be adjusted based on how your body responds and your blood counts. Never change your dose or take it more often without talking to your doctor first. Because capsules come in different strengths, your pharmacist may give you a combination of capsules to make up your total dose — take ALL of them together as instructed.
missed_dose: Because lomustine is taken only once every 6 weeks, contact your doctor or nurse right away if you miss your scheduled dose or forget to take it. Do NOT take an extra dose on your own to make up for a missed one. Your doctor will tell you when it is safe to reschedule your dose.
storage: Store lomustine capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Return any unused capsules to your pharmacist for proper disposal — do not throw them in the trash or flush them down the toilet.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who have infections, colds, or the flu, as lomustine lowers your immune system and makes it harder to fight germs. Do not get any live vaccines (such as live flu vaccine, shingles vaccine, or MMR) while taking this medicine without asking your doctor first. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can increase nausea and may interact with the medication. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child during treatment and for a period of time after, as lomustine can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control. Women should not breastfeed while taking this medication. Caregivers should wear gloves when handling the capsules to avoid skin contact.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, unusual bruising or bleeding, blood in urine or stool, extreme tiredness or weakness, shortness of breath or persistent cough, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), severe nausea or vomiting that you cannot control, signs of infection (redness, swelling, pain), confusion or changes in thinking, mouth sores that are severe or prevent eating, or if you accidentally take more than your prescribed dose. Also call your doctor before each new cycle to review your blood test results.
when_it_works: Lomustine works slowly over time. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular blood tests and imaging scans (such as MRI or CT scans). It may take several treatment cycles before you or your doctor see results. It is important to keep all of your follow-up appointments so your doctor can check how well the medicine is working and adjust your care if needed.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Lomustine can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Women of childbearing age must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 2 years after the last dose. Men should use contraception for at least 4 months after treatment. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Older adults (65+): Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially low blood counts. Close monitoring is important. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver disease. Children: Lomustine can be used in children for certain cancers under close medical supervision. Doses are carefully calculated based on the child's body size.
